item.title: Dreesen sends clear message on Bayern-Haaland links
item.description: Dreesen sends clear message on Bayern-Haaland links With Manchester City facing the consequences of 115 alleged breaches of the Premier League's financial rules, it has been suggested that the club could even be relegated as punishment. Should that happen, many of the Premier League giants' star players, including Erling Haaland, could find themselves on the move. Bayern Munich were linked with the Norwegian international before he joined Borussia Dortmund and later moved to Manchester City. However, according to the German champions' CEO, Jan-Christian Dreesen, there's no interest in reviving their pursuit of the striker at the moment. “We have Harry Kane, the best striker in the world, and an attacking line-up that is second to none in Europe. So this is not a question we even need to consider,” Dreesen told Die Welt. Asked whether Bayern could even afford Haaland given his lucrative contract at Manchester City, Dreesen responded: “We have shown that we can sign players from the Premier League, not only with Harry Kane, but also with Luis Díaz and Michael Olise. We have a wonderful team with a mix of players that we are very happy with.”

item.title: Carlo Ancelotti confirms why Alisson didn’t make the Brazil squad
item.description: Carlo Ancelotti confirms why Alisson didn’t make the Brazil squad Brazil Squad Rebuild Continues with Alisson Omission for November Friendlies Carlo Ancelotti has made the point clearly enough. Brazil are rebuilding, and sentiment is not part of the process. His latest squad for November friendlies against Japan and Singapore is packed with youth, short on established names in certain areas, and designed with 2027 and beyond in mind. Brazil meet Japan in Singapore on November 14, before facing Singapore three days later. For a national side still dealing with the hangover of a poor 2026 World Cup, these games are not about prestige. They are about sorting through options, cutting through reputation and working out who can help form the next serious Brazil team. Carlo Ancelotti pushes Brazil rebuild The numbers tell the story. Nine players are of Olympic age, while 15 are under 23. That is not a nod to youth, it is a deliberate strategy. Ancelotti said: “During this period leading up to 2027, we must carry out this work to find a clear direction.” He then laid out the timeline with little room for confusion: “I believe that by the first friendly matches of 2028, as the [World Cup] qualifiers begin and preparations for the Copa America get underway, we’ll have a more established team. We need to make the most of 2027 to carry out this renewal.” That is as blunt as it gets. Brazil are using friendlies as a laboratory, and there is logic in that. The old cycle ended badly. This one starts with risk, turnover and plenty of rough edges. Alisson omission suits Liverpool and Brazil Alisson Becker is again absent, and no, this is not a demotion. Ancelotti has chosen Bento, Lucas Perri and Pedro Morisco as his three goalkeepers, using the window to assess depth rather than revisit what he already knows. “We don’t need to test Alisson [for example],” he said. “We know him very well. He is the best goalkeeper. “When the Copa America begins, he will be called up, and it’s the same for the others. Right now, it’s time to observe, refresh the squad, and help young players reach their full potential.” For Liverpool, the upside is obvious. Alisson avoids a long trip to Southeast Asia and stays put during the international break. For Brazil, the logic is straightforward too. You already know your number one. The question is who sits behind him. Brazil squad shows youth-first direction The squad includes Endrick, Vinícius Júnior, Estêvão, Rayan and Andrey Santos, names that fit the broader Brazil rebuild, alongside senior figures such as Raphinha, Gabriel Magalhães and Bruno Guimarães. It is a group built less for immediate certainty and more for evaluation. That may frustrate those wanting quick fixes, but Brazil are not pretending otherwise. The reset is happening now, and Ancelotti has made his priorities obvious.

item.title: Ex-captain says club was turned into 'dictatorship'
item.description: Emily Owen spent four years playing at Cheltenham [Shutterstock] The former captain of Cheltenham Town's women's side has accused "an individual" of turning the club into "a dictatorship where players feel psychologically unsafe". On Monday, Emily Owen announced she was to depart the Women's National League Southern Premier side after four years, during which she made more than 130 appearances. But following the club sharing the news on social media, the defender posted a message to say she had left due to "a lack of an individual's principles and outright failures in processes". Cheltenham Town Women said while it would not comment on individual cases, it takes all matters relating to the welfare and wellbeing of its players "extremely seriously". Owen said she "wanted to set the record straight" after hearing of rumours circulating around the reasons for her departure. "One individual in particular has far too much control within this team, turning the environment into a dictatorship where players feel psychologically unsafe," she said. She went on to claim three other players had left the club "on moral grounds as boundaries were crossed, that shouldn't be crossed in women's football". A spokesperson for Cheltenham Town Women said: "Cheltenham Town Women are committed to ensuring that every player, member of staff and volunteer is treated with respect and feels safe, valued and supported within our environment. "We will ensure that any concerns brought to our attention are treated appropriately, sensitively and in line with all relevant policies and procedures". All the latest Cheltenham Town news

item.title: Dart stuns Badosa to make second career semi-final
item.description: Harriet Dart is ranked 115th in the world [Getty Images] Britain's Harriet Dart reached the second WTA Tour semi-final of her career when she fought back from a set down to beat fifth seed Paula Badosa at the Guangzhou Open in China. The 30-year-old triumphed 3-6 6-2 6-4 against Spain's Badosa - ranked 54 places above her - in two hours and 15 minutes at Nansha International Tennis Centre. Dart's first appearance in the semi-finals of a tour event came at the Transylvania Open in Cluj-Napoca, where she lost in straight sets to Karolina Pliskova. She will face either American Claire Liu or 16-year-old Chinese wildcard Sun Xinran in the last four on Saturday. "It's been a very long time since I've been in the business end of the tournament so I am really excited for that," Dart said. "Tennis is so stressful, so to have the opportunity to compete again on Saturday is a great opportunity for me." Dart, who came through qualifying and beat second-seed Janice Tjen in the previous round, lost her opening service game in the first set but broke back and draw level at 3-3. However, Badosa broke Dart's serve again to take a 5-3 lead and held her serve to close out the set. The pair exchanged breaks at the start of the second set before Dart seized the upper hand to clinch the set. Badosa, who required two medical timeouts during the match as she appeared to struggle with the heat, saved a match point at 5-3 in the deciding set and then breaking Dart's serve. But the Spaniard, ranked 61st in the world, was running on empty in her next service game, as Dart won it to love. "It was an incredible battle. I thought Paula started really strongly. I was always behind, and knew it was going to be an incredibly tough match," Dart added. "I really needed to hang in there during the tough moments and wait for a chance. Luckily I was able to take my chance, and I am very excited to be in the semi-finals." item.title: Why Justin Herbert, 3 other NFL stars won't be traded: Follow the money
item.description: As the NFL’s Nov. 10 deadline for teams to execute trades draws closer, the ever-industrious rumor mill is bound to generate some fanciful suppositions, suggestions and theories. But in a football reality governed by a salary cap and contract parameters, some of the proposed deals floating around in the ether need to be taken with a serious grain of salt. Some contracts, even for superstar-caliber performers, are constructed in such a way to make them transferrable − former Titans' DT Jeffery Simmons' arrangement a prime example . Yet some teams simply can’t afford to take on certain players’ pacts and, conversely, there are other squads that would be extremely challenged to move some of their own guys due to the cap consequences. These four stars are highly unlikely to be dealt due to their contractual circumstances: Philadelphia Eagles RB Saquon Barkley One of Philly’s team captains, he valiantly played though his hamstring injury – and hurt his back in the process – while trying to help salvage the Eagles’ season in Monday night’s loss to the Dallas Cowboys. Given Barkley is well shy of 100%, teams in need of a back who can alter the scales might be better off pursuing the Indianapolis Colts’ Jonathan Taylor or Tennessee Titans ’ Tony Pollard. But if Barkley does wind up on the trade block, he’s going to be hard for EVP/GM Howie Roseman to spin off anyway. Trading Barkley would mean a dead cap charge of approximately $26 million for the Eagles in 2027 – when the recent trades of WR A.J. Brown and OL Cam Jurgens alone are already going to cost Philadelphia $42 million in dead money. Adding to that figure, especially given the uncertainty surrounding QB Jalen Hurts, may not be a pragmatic choice for Roseman … unless he gets an unlikely godfather offer for the 2024 Offensive Player of the Year. “You can’t control it,” Barkley said Monday night of the trade speculation starting to billow around the team. “That’s part of the business.” THREE CONTRACTS THAT ARE EASY TO MOVE: Including Maxx Crosby's huge deal Los Angeles Chargers QB Justin Herbert Whether from a financial, political or public relations standpoint, moving a franchise quarterback in the prime of his career is almost certainly not going to be easy. item.title: Framingham Turkey Classic race returns for charity
item.description: The 31st annual Turkey Classic Road Race will bring runners to Framingham on Nov. 26 for a 3.1-mile race that will benefit Veterans SOAR and other local charities. The race begins at 8 a.m., according to a community announcement. The course starts and finishes at the Framingham Police Department, with race activities based in the parking lot of the Memorial Building, 150 Concord St. The event is sponsored by the Framingham Fire Department Local 1652 and Framingham Police Association. Proceeds will benefit Veterans SOAR, which provides services to veterans in the MetroWest area, and other local charities. The entry fee is $40 and is nonrefundable. Long-sleeve T-shirts will be available while supplies last. Registration is limited to the first 1,000 runners and will close Oct. 31 or earlier if the race reaches capacity. There will be no race-day registration. Number pickup, awards and race divisions Runners can pick up their numbers Nov. 25 from 1 to 4 p.m. at the Framingham Elks, 450 Union Ave., or before 7:45 a.m. on race day at the Memorial Building. A $100 cash prize will go to the overall top male and female finishers. The announcement also lists prizes for top male and female finishers in race categories. Categories are 10 and under, 11-15, 16-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70-79 and 80 and older. Wheelchair and police/fire divisions are also offered. The event announcement also lists food, refreshments, Table Talk Pies, Poland Spring water and a raffle among the race activities. item.title: ‘Nobody wants to…’ – Travis Hunter reveals if he intentionally used a fake stumble on CJ Stroud
item.description: Photo by James Gilbert/Getty Images Travis Hunter has denied deliberately pretending to stumble to trick Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud into throwing an interception during the Jacksonville Jaguars’ recent defeat. The Jaguars rookie became the centre of attention after intercepting Stroud in the end zone, with viral social media posts claiming he had intentionally made himself look off balance to fool the quarterback. Hunter has now addressed the speculation, insisting he never claimed to use such a tactic and explaining what he was trying to do on the play. Travis Hunter shuts down fake stumble claims after viral interception Speaking to reporters, Hunter said: “No, I’ve never said that. I don’t know. They just be making up stuff. I’ve never said that. Nobody wants to stumble and try to make it look like something it’s not. My coach told me to burn, so I felt like I was me. I put my eyes down and got to the minute as fast as I can.” The rumours gained traction after NFL insider Dov Kleiman and other social media accounts suggested Hunter had previously explained how he used fake stumbles to deceive quarterbacks. However, the reference material indicates the claims stemmed from posts interpreting his previous interviews rather than a confirmed admission from the Jaguars star. Hunter’s interception came during a dramatic fourth quarter against Houston. After catching a seven-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence to bring Jacksonville within three points, the cornerback intercepted Stroud in the end zone on the Texans’ next possession. The Jaguars eventually lost 34-31, but Hunter’s performance highlighted his ability to contribute on both sides of the ball. He finished the game with four receptions for 59 yards and a touchdown, alongside the interception that gave Jacksonville another opportunity to complete their comeback. Hunter’s performance also arrived amid wider scrutiny over his role in Jacksonville. The second overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft has faced criticism over his limited offensive workload, with the Jaguars prioritising his development as a cornerback. Offensive coordinator Grant Udinski has explained that Hunter’s involvement as a receiver will vary from game to game as the team looks to develop his skill set while managing his defensive responsibilities. Jacksonville will now prepare for its next matchup against the Indianapolis Colts, with Hunter’s growing role and recent performance likely to remain talking points. item.title: New variations, angles and better accuracy helping Kotian trouble batters
item.description: MUMBAI: Competing neck and neck with Madhya Pradesh's off-spinner Saransh Jain, Tanush Kotian is doing his best to stay in the race and in the radar of national selectors. On Thursday, the 28-year-old took a career-best eight for 81 in 34.3 overs in the second innings against Haryana. Having taken three for 70 in 30.5 overs in the first innings, Kotian finished with match figures of 11 for 151. His effort helped Mumbai register their third consecutive bonus-point win of the season, as they beat Haryana by 10 wickets at the MCA ground in BKC on the fourth and final day of their Ranji Trophy Elite Group D match. The match was a special one for Kotian as it was his 50th first-class appearance. He marked the occasion with his first 10-wicket haul in a match and his fourth five-wicket haul. "I have had four years of progress and improvement in my bowling. I did a lot of tours, I was also with the India team. They all guided me a lot, like I was practising with (BCCI COE spin bowing coach) Sunil Joshi sir, Jatin (Paranjape) sir and Rajesh (Sanil) sir (childhood coach and mentor). A lot of people have guided me. I am trying to use that experience in my bowling," Kotian told reporters after the match. The off-spinner, who took three for 30 against Chandigarh in Mumbai's opening match of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season, said he had worked on his line and length, added new variations and tried different angles to trouble batters. "I have improved a lot in line and length. I have brought in two-three variations which are helping me in deceiving and beating the batsman. I am trying to do that in every match and working on my accuracy as well. I have worked on different angles. Sometimes when I was bowling from over the wicket to the lefty, I was using angles and crease and it looked better as I was not allowing the batters to get set. It was helping me in creating pressure on the batsmen and doubts in their minds," he said. Explaining what worked for him against Haryana, Kotian said he focused on bowling in the right areas and asked for specific field placements to support his plans. "I was looking to bowl in good areas and the field set-up that I needed, I was specifically asking for it and bowling accordingly. I was able to create opportunities and was in a good rhythm." Kotian also scored his 20th first-class half-century in Mumbai's first innings. He said he had been working on improving his batting while focusing on accuracy with the ball. "I have worked on myself. In batting, I’m trying to contribute in the lower order and improve further but in bowling, I feel that I've worked a lot on my accuracy. I feel that's the key. I'm accurately bowling at the right place. I’m also talking to the ‘keeper as to how it is going and I am happy with that," he said. item.title: Carlos Tevez says move to Manchester City was 'revenge' after Ferguson broke promises
item.description: Carlos Tevez says move to Manchester City was 'revenge' after Ferguson broke promises Carlos Tevez has said his controversial move to Manchester City was revenge for broken promises during his time at rivals Manchester United . Tevez made one of the most infamous moves in Premier League history when he crossed the Manchester divide to sign for City in 2009. The Argentina international had been a big favourites at Manchester United, where he won two league titles, a League Cup, and the Champions League. United had signed Tevez on an initial two-year loan deal, and he has now revealed how broken promises over a permanent move saw him leave Old Trafford. Speaking to former teammate Rio Ferdinand, Tevez said his relationship with Sir Alex Ferguson broke down after the former United manager failed 'to keep his word'. Tevez signed for Manchester City in 2009 and scored 73 goals in 148 games, winning a third Premier League title in 2011/12. During the title celebrations, he famously held up a 'RIP Fergie' banner. Tevez explained the events that led to his controversial move and believes the United fans 'understand' his decision. “Fergie didn’t keep his word”: Tevez explains the broken promise behind his move to Man City “For me it was hard. It was hard because I felt like I'd given my heart to United. And I didn't feel the same,' he said to Rio Ferdinand Presents. “They spoke to me before the two-year loan. After, if you play well, we pay the contract after one year. “Fergie told me, ‘Carlos, now I'm going to pay out your contract and you're going to stay in Manchester’. “The team went to a pre-season. I remember this conversation with Fergie. He said ‘I’m going to pay for [Dimitar] Berbatov but you, don't worry, I'm going to buy you and we'll do your contract. “For me, the people [United fans] understand. item.title: Tottenham Hotspur defender responds to Barcelona transfer links: ‘Would love to return to Spain’
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur defender responds to Barcelona transfer links: ‘Would love to return to Spain’ Barcelona’s defensive problems have been compounded by recent injuries at the back. Currently, Hansi Flick is without Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen and Xavi Espart, with all four out injured. This leaves the German manager with just four first-team defensive options: Joao Cancelo, Pau Cubarsi, Gerard Martin and Alejandro Balde. This has prompted discussion about potential reinforcements for Barcelona, with Pedro Porro one of the names on the radar. Despite Joan Laporta’s reported admiration for the Spaniard, the Catalans are unlikely to make a move for him in January. Speaking to Cadena SER’s El Larguero , Porro addressed his future and admitted that he would welcome a return to Spanish football. Pedro Porro opens door to a return to Spain The 27-year-old made it clear that he remains committed to Tottenham, having signed a new contract before the 2026 World Cup. Nevertheless, the prospect of returning home continues to appeal to him. Pedro Porro is reportedly on Barcelona’s radar. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) “I would love to return to Spain,” Porro admitted, explaining that playing in his homeland remains an exciting possibility. However, the Spanish international also played down reports suggesting that Barcelona or Madrid had made serious attempts to sign him. “Nobody has told me Barcelona or Madrid want me,” he revealed, explaining that enquiries about his situation never developed into concrete interest. When asked which of the two Spanish giants would better suit his playing style, Porro avoided choosing a side. “I consider myself a player who can adapt to anything,” he responded. Barcelona unlikely to pursue expensive deal Despite his openness to returning to La Liga , a move to Barcelona currently appears unlikely. Transfer expert Matteo Moretto recently revealed that the Catalans are not actively pursuing Porro. His substantial salary and Tottenham’s financial demands are seen as major obstacles. Pedro Porro wants to return to Spain in the future. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) The Spaniard’s contract runs until 2031, further complicating matters. Tottenham are said to want more than €60 million. Porro’s attacking qualities would certainly appeal to Hansi Flick, particularly his crossing and ability to support the right winger. However, with Jules Kounde, Eric Garcia, Xavi Espart and Joao Cancelo already at the club, investing heavily in another right-back may not represent the smartest use of limited resources. Instead, what Barça need immediately is a new centre-back to add some bite to that position, and that is where the focus needs to be. It remains to be seen how Pedro Porro’s time at Spurs pans out and whether Barcelona consider a move for him in the future.

item.title: 'My bike only works in a straight line,' says frustrated Francesco Bagnaia after Malaysian GP practice
item.description: Motorsport photo Francesco Bagnaia has called his situation "ridiculous" after failing to make it directly into Q2 for this weekend's MotoGP Malaysian Grand Prix. While the double world champion had already failed to make the Friday cut 10 times in 2026, his excellent record in Malaysia meant he came into this event with a lot more confidence. Even amid the horrors of his 2025 campaign, he had been fast at Sepang and won the sprint race from pole. Read Also: Francesco Bagnaia calls Sepang his “best chance” and vows to “risk more” But he was left frustrated after this year's opening day did not go to plan for the factory Ducati rider. He found himself outside the critical top 10 with just minutes remaining in the practice session, then crashed as he looked to make the cut. Although he fell at Turn 1, Bagnaia said the fast first and fourth sectors were not the problem when it came to putting together a lap time. "My bike works only when it's straight, so I did the maximum in the first and last sector," he reported. "I think I'm in the top three in both sectors. In the other two sectors I lose eight tenths, so it's ridiculous." Indeed, Bagnaia was second-quickest in sector one and third-quickest in sector four. These parts of the track include the two main straights, where his Ducati was performing well. He was the fastest representative from Borgo Panigale in the top-speed charts, joining several other riders with the second-fastest recorded maximum. Francesco Bagnaia, Ducati Team Francesco Bagnaia, Ducati Team The 'ideal lap time', which combines all a rider's best sectors, would also have only put Bagnaia in the 12th position he managed in reality, suggesting he had not left a lot out there. Bagnaia was not in a chatty mood after the session, and responded as follows when asked about the performance of different aero options: "To feel something, you need to have a feeling on the bike." He did not choose to blame circuit conditions for his misfortune on a day when the track appeared slippery. Sepang hosted a rare Formula 1 race earlier this month, and had been due for a resurface ahead of this year's MotoGP race - only for the work not to be done after all. "The track feels like in the [pre-season] test," he said. "We need the resurface, but they were trying to do it, but unluckily they could not ship the material here to do it. So we already knew that it was the last time riding in these conditions. "[But] my feeling on the bike is completely different. So this is the main thing to understand, but more or less all the season it has been like this." item.description: Marotta: Inter and Milan need new stadium to fill ‘big gap’ with European rivals Inter President Beppe Marotta says the new San Siro will be an asset and a ‘source of revenue’ for the Nerazzurri and Milan as the Milanese sides aim to fill the ‘big gap’ with European rivals. Inter and Milan unveiled the new San Siro project on Thursday . It will have a capacity of 71,5000 and be called ‘Generali Stadium’ for the next 20 years. “In some respects, whilst San Siro represents a repository of historical memory, it no longer meets the requirements of a modern stadium or what the fans want,” Marotta told The Athletic. PISA, ITALY – NOVEMBER 30: Giuseppe Marotta of FC Internazionale looks on prior to the Serie A match between Pisa SC and FC Internazionale at Arena Garibaldi on November 30, 2025 in Pisa, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) The new stadium will be adjacent to the existing Stadio Meazza, meaning that Inter and Milan will continue playing in their current stadium until the new one is ready. Work will begin in 2028, and the stadium will be ready for the 2031-32 season, just in time for Euro 2032, which Italy will co-host with Turkiye. “Just consider that, according to the figures we have today, Real Madrid generates around €250m a year (from the Bernabeu), whilst we’re currently just under €100m with San Siro. As well as being an asset for the club, a stadium is also a source of revenue,” Marotta continued. A view of the design inside the Generali Stadium, where Inter and AC Milan will have their own ‘Curva’ to replace San Siro (acmilan.com) “At present, there’s far too big a gap between us in Italy and some of our rival clubs in Europe, which also affects our competitiveness and certainly puts us in a very difficult position.” Like every modern stadium in the world, activities at Inter and Milan’s new stadium won’t only be limited to football matches. “A stadium must have a life of its own and be functional, not just on Sundays or when matches are played,” Marotta argued. “In Italy, where there are major bureaucratic hurdles to launching projects of this nature, this has come about thanks in part to the arrival and tenacity of Oaktree. MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: General view of the outside of the stadium before the Serie A match between AC Milan and US Lecce at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 20, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) “Their tenacity has perhaps broken down some of the bureaucratic barriers which, in our country, unfortunately represented a major stumbling block and were difficult to overcome. Today, we are truly on an upward trajectory.” Inter and Milan will meet in the Derby della Madonnina tomorrow, Saturday, October 31. item.title: Bayern send clear message on signing Erling Haaland
item.description: Bayern send clear message on signing Erling Haaland Erling Haaland is not currently a transfer topic at Bayern Munich. Multiple reports have been keen to link the Norwegian international with a switch to the Bundesliga champions. However, FC Bayern CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen was clear that the Bavarians are satisfied with their offensive options. Bayern are happy with Harry Kane – and why shouldn’t they be? (Photo by Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images) Nothing will change FC Bayern’s mind on the matter – not even the impending outcome of Man City’s appeal against the 114 charges landed against them with the Premier League’s investigation into their financial wrongdoing. “I spoke to Bayern CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen on the topic of Erling Haaland and the message coming from the club is pretty clear: FC Bayern won’t go for Erling Haaland,” Christian Falk exclusively informed CF Bayern Insider . “He told me that, with Harry Kane, the club already has the best striker in world football . Not to mention a great offensive line overall! “So Bayern Munich won’t move for Haaland – regardless of the outcome of the Sky Blues’ appeal following the Premier League’s investigation into their reported financial doping.” And why should it? In Harry Kane, Bayern Munich have the best striker in world football – the world’s leading footballer, if the Ballon d’Or voting results are anything to go by. The England international is an exceptional footballer who can’t merely be defined by his goalscoring. He drops deep, he supports build-up and provides a playmaking interpretation of the central striker role of the likes of which arguably has never been witnessed before. Yes, there is the age disparity, with seven years separating Haaland (26) from his Bayern counterpart (33). But in a league where Kane’s legs and body are protected, the England skipper’s twilight years look set to extend deeper into his 30s. Could Haaland be the eventual succession plan? (Photo by Matt McNulty/Getty Images) To a certain extent, Bayern have to be wary about any potential pursuit of the Manchester City hitman. While unquestionably a freakishly brilliant goalscorer, signing the footballer would represent a significant shift for Bayern’s forward line. The wide options, whatever they look like in however many years, would need to take on more of a facilitating role for starters. But there’s a wider issue that would need to be addressed, which is the drop in build-up quality and creativity. Who is stepping into Harry Kane’s boots to provide playmaking options from deep? Can anyone else ask questions of the opponent’s backline from within their own defensive half as Kane can? It’s not as simple as replacing the Englishman’s goals. Goals, ultimately, come and go; it’s the Bayern Munich striker’s excellence on the ball that will be considerably more difficult to replace, never mind replicate elsewhere on the pitch.

The off-road adventure begins on January 9 in the Algarve. Two days later, the participants cross the Mediterranean by ship to Morocco. The rally ends in Marrakesh on January 23 after 7,824 kilometres. It marks the event's return to African soil for the first time since 2007. The annual Dakar Rally originally went from Paris to Dakar, but safety concerns in the Sahel meant it moved to South America in 2009 and then switched to Saudi Arabia in 2020. item.description: Almost 70 years ago, two students met at Ohio State’s main library. They were student employees, introduced by a sister-in-law who was working as a supervisor. Even from different floors of the library, they became inseparable. Rosemary Gorman, according to family lore, would call Robert Fahey’s floor just to hear his voice. The young couple dated for a year before marrying in 1958 and settling in California. Fahey was an industrial engineer and got a job as a defense contractor with Douglas Aircraft, which was based in Santa Monica. The move took them almost 2,000 miles from Columbus, but it did little to diminish their devotion to their alma mater. They watched the Buckeyes whenever their games aired on one of the three television networks. They took the children to the 1971 Rose Bowl when Ohio State played Stanford. Their son, Steve, revered Rex Kern, the quarterback who led the Buckeyes to the national title as a sophomore in 1968. The attachment to Ohio State endured over the decades, like a family heirloom passed down through generations. It would eventually be inherited by their grandson. Luke Fahey might have been raised in Orange County, but he carried the same fondness for the Buckeyes. In a sea of USC and UCLA fans, the ties only strengthened as Ohio State won a national championship in 2014 and remained one of the country’s dominant programs. “Luke grew up with the idea of being a Buckeye and contributing to the team,” said Luke's father, Steve Fahey. “That was the hugest thing to him. I don't want to sound too corny, but it's the truth.” He will have the opportunity on Oct. 31 when the Buckeyes return from their idle week to play at USC without starting quarterback Julian Sayin, who is out indefinitely after he was injured in their win at Indiana . While coach Ryan Day declined to announce a starter in the days leading up to kickoff, Fahey is seen as most likely to be behind center following a midseason competition with Tavien St. Clair as the Buckeyes look to remain at the forefront of the Big Ten race and College Football Playoff hunt. item.description: Watch: 'I made the wrong decision,' Hyrox athlete Joanna Wietrzyk tells BBC An Australian athlete has admitted making the wrong decision and putting others at risk by continuing to race after soiling herself during an endurance sports event. Speaking exclusively to the BBC ahead of her return to the sport, Joanna Wietrzyk suggested her determination to win the Hyrox race in Beijing in September had clouded her judgement: "It was my decision to continue racing so I take full responsibility for that." Challenged over why she carried on, she said: "I didn't really think about those around me… the decision that I made in hindsight was the wrong decision and I'm truly sorry for everyone that I did affect." The 24-year-old said that the experience and subsequent backlash was "traumatic". She also said she had considered walking away from the sport, in which she holds a world record. Hyrox sees participants alternate between running a kilometre and doing fitness exercises, including a sled push, burpee jumps, indoor rowing, and lunges while carrying a sandbag. The competition has exploded in popularity since it was founded in 2017 in Hamburg, in northern Germany, and is now held across the world. Wietrzyk said she had suffered a bacterial infection from food poisoning [Getty Images] Roughly halfway through her event last month, Wietrzyk suffered a bout of diarrhoea. Images of faecal matter on parts of her body were then shared widely online. Asked whether officials should have stopped her, she said no-one encouraged her to do so at the time. Hyrox's co-founder, Moritz Fürste, has issued an apology saying it had been a mistake not to react immediately during the race. New rules have now been introduced giving race directors the power to remove athletes if their vomit, urine or faeces pose a risk of contamination or threaten the welfare of themselves or others in a race that is primarily held indoors using shared equipment. Although initially defiant in a now-deleted Instagram post, Wietrzyk apologised in the week after the Beijing event and said she would forfeit the win and retroactively withdraw from the race. Due to compete in Hamburg on Friday, she said she was "nervous" about her return and hoped that the high-profile incident would not define her. "I don't want it to become my identity," she said. item.title: Michael Carrick is facing a familiar Man United problem – but Chelsea clash could offer a way out
item.description: As Michael Carrick and Xabi Alonso both try to come up with gameplans for Saturday’s hugely significant first – and potentially last – meeting as coaches, both have felt an inclination to look back at when they met across the centre circle rather than the dug-outs. They used to try and out-think each other on the pitch, after all. Alonso was always struck by one quality. The former Liverpool midfielder found that Carrick just had an apparently innate ability to see where play was going. “Somebody who knows how to be in the right place at the right time,” as Alonso put it back in 2010. Michael Carrick surprisingly survived the sack this week but remains under huge pressure (Reuters) Those words seem all the more jarring now since Carrick finds himself going to Chelsea amid a widespread belief that Manchester United have made the wrong decision in keeping him in the role. Wrong place, wrong time. Directing the play on the pitch has so far come a lot easier to both former midfielders than directing play off it. And yet that entire era when they were at their peaks, from around 2006 right through to 2013 and Alonso’s own moves to Real Madrid and Bayern Munich, offers a further poignancy for both clubs precisely because of the many pictures of celebration. It could be felt this week as Carrick was serenaded by the Old Trafford crowd because of his contributions to the club’s history, while everyone else was booed. Michael Carrick retains some support from the Manchester United fans (PA Wire) There’s even the more challenging concept of how the successes of those days played into the travails of now. For Chelsea, Roman Abramovich’s proximity to Vladimir Putin ensured his removal was ultimately inevitable. Trophies came at a considerable cost, with many of them a consequence of cheating comparable to Manchester City that should have seen them stripped of titles. Alonso has inherited a club still figuring out a modern identity. For United, it’s the way Sir Alex Ferguson’s singular ability to adapt to the Glazer ownership left the wider club ill-equipped to deal with what next. They’re figuring out much more than an identity. Despite fair criticism of Carrick as a coach, he has been left in a more challenging situation than any of his modern predecessors. And that’s inevitably left him facing a familiar crisis that submerged all of them, too. David Moyes had it almost immediately. Louis van Gaal had it in the winter of 2015. Jose Mourinho endured it from early 2018, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in mid-2021. Erik ten Hag had it from the start of the 2023-24 season and Carrick from the start of this one. None ever fully recovered. item.title: First images released of 71,000-seater replacement for iconic European football stadium
item.description: More than a century after it was opened, Milan’s took another step towards its demise on Thursday, paving the way for the Generali Stadium. At the historic Castello Sforzesco, AC Milan and Inter Milan revealed joint proposals for a new venue, which would see the demolition of the Stadio Giuseppe Meazza, commonly known as the San Siro. The two football clubs, who have long shared their ground, have already secured a naming rights deal, with the replacement arena named Generali Stadium after Italy ’s largest insurance firm. Prior to the briefing, Inter supporters staged a protest in the castle courtyard, unfurling a banner reading "you will never extinguish the lights at San Siro" while chanting "hands off San Siro." Here’s some more things to know about Milan’s new stadium: The architects The clubs had already announced agreements last year with architectural firms Foster + Partners and Manica to design a new stadium. Foster + Partners and Manica’s projects include Wembley Stadium in London, Chase Center in San Francisco, and Lusail Stadium in Qatar. AC Milan and Inter Milan revealed joint proposals for a new venue, which would see the demolition of the Stadio Giuseppe Meazza, commonly known as the San Siro (Foster + Partners) Norman Foster and David Manica presented the plans at Thursday’s briefing. “It is always a challenge to design a building that replaces a beloved project,” Manica said. “And the way I’m thinking about this project and the spirit that we began with from the beginning was: same soul, different building. “The most important thing that we realiSed when we designed this project is that the San Siro is a feeling, more than a building, it’s a feeling. And everything that we needed to do here was to drive that feeling and carry it into the building.” The structure At the heart of the design is a striking oval form, with the frame of the stadium made out of 80 huge diamond shapes and a sweeping double-curved roof. The diamond shapes offer glimpses into the stadium from the outside and sweeping views across the city from within. The points of the diamonds are the tallest — 60 meters — at each of the ends behind the goals, known as “the curva” in Italian, where the hard-core fans normally sit. “How do you take the legend of San Siro and how do you build on that? Perhaps the essence are the fans at the two extreme ends behind the goal, ‘the curve’,” Foster said. “And in the new stadium, look at the shape of it, it’s low in the body and it rises up at either end, and that’s the response to the fans.” The stadium will be raised on a podium, with space underneath for parking, a museum and club stores. The 360-degree stadium bowl will have 71,500 seats across two tiers — in comparison to the three ‘rings’ of San Siro.
